transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Um... well, I just feel like I can't settle inside my own skin anymore. Even when I'm completely worn out and I know I should just be sitting still, I just... I feel like I have to jump up and do the next thing. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, especially any antipsychotics or other psychiatric medications?
No. Um... I haven't started anything new. Or changed anything. Just... no.

When you feel this need to keep moving, is it mainly a physical, restless feeling in your legs or body, or is it more that your mind is racing with worried or speeded-up thoughts that make you want to get up and do something?
I... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. It's just... I just feel like I need to get up. I couldn't tell you if it's my legs or my head. I'm just not sure.
Does this restless feeling mainly happen when you're trying to sit or lie still, and does getting up and moving around actually make it feel better?

Um... no, I wouldn't say that. It's not just when I'm trying to sit or lie down. It's... kind of always there. And getting up doesn't really make it go away or feel better. I just... I just do it anyway.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling unusually sad, down, or hopeless, or alternatively unusually elevated, irritable, or 'on top of the world'?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't felt sad or... or anything like that. Just... no, not really.

Thinking back, would you say you've had this kind of restlessness and trouble sitting still since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only started more recently, like in the past few months?

Um... since I was a kid, I suppose. It's not a new thing. Even back in grade school, my teachers... they used to write that I was bright, but careless. I was always losing my papers. And... talking out of turn. They always had to remind me to just stay in my seat and finish my work. So... yeah. Always.
These days, do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, and do you often lose track of things or forget appointments at both work and at home?

Um... yes, I suppose. I just... I forget things a lot. Ordinary things. Like, I'll forget to call my daughter back, or... paying a bill until I get a late notice. And if I say I'll bring a folder to a meeting, I usually forget it. It just happens.
Would you say these problems with restlessness and forgetfulness have actually caused real difficulties for you—like at work, in your relationships, or managing daily responsibilities at home?

Um... yes. I suppose it has. 

My family... they've had to step in lately. With the bills and... the paperwork. And... well, at my church, and the garden... I've dropped some things. People had to cover for me, or redo the plans. 

It's... um. It's embarrassing. I just... I don't think those groups feel they can really count on me anymore.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports lifelong (since childhood) symptoms of inattention (losing items, forgetfulness, difficulty finishing tasks, careless errors noted by teachers) and hyperactivity/restlessness (inability to sit still, urge to move despite exhaustion) that are pervasive across multiple settings (home, work, church, garden club) and cause clear functional impairment (family managing bills/paperwork, others covering responsibilities). The restlessness is not confined to sitting/lying still, is not relieved by movement, and there is no recent medication change or antipsychotic exposure, making akathisia (G25.71) unlikely. No mood elevation, depression, or anxiety symptoms are endorsed, arguing against a mood or anxiety disorder as the primary driver of restlessness. The combination of chronic inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms since childhood with cross-situational impairment supports a diagnosis of ADHD, combined presentation (F90.0).
